Class OidcUserinfoEndpoint

java.lang.Object
iu.oidc.provider.OidcUserinfoEndpoint
public class OidcUserinfoEndpoint extends Object
Answers the OpenID Connect UserInfo request.

Reads an access token this provider issued, asks a claims source what it holds about the principal that token names, and answers what the grant's scope admits — signed and encrypted as the client registered.

What this owns, and what it doesn't

The three things here are the three an identity service has no business doing. It cannot verify this provider's tokens; it doesn't know which relying party is asking, so it cannot decide which claims that party may see; and it holds neither this provider's signing keys nor the client's encryption key. So an IuOidcClaimsSource answers what it knows about a principal and nothing more, and stays free of OpenID Connect entirely.

Rendering claims as JSON isn't here either. What a source answers renders itself, so this publishes toString() without looking at it — which keeps the module free of any opinion about how a claim prints, including the two a general-purpose converter gets wrong, updated_at being a NumericDate and address being nested.

The subject is checked against the token

A source is told which principal to answer about and must answer that principal's name back as sub. This checks rather than trusting: a relying party matches sub against the ID token it holds and refuses the response when the two disagree, so a source that resolves a principal name to some other form — a username for a numeric ID, say — would break that comparison silently. Checking is all that is available now that the document renders itself; there is no longer a view in between to bind the claim from.

    • userinfo

      public OidcUserinfoResult userinfo(String accessToken)
      Answers a UserInfo request.
      Parameters:
      accessToken - bearer token presented, as the transport read it out of the Authorization header
      Returns:
      the response, and what to call it
      Throws:
      SecurityException - if the access token can't be verified, or its registered claims don't hold; a caller answers invalid_token
      IllegalStateException - if the claims source answers about somebody other than the principal it was asked about
      NullPointerException - if this provider or the client is configured for something it hasn't supplied a key for, or the claims source answers nothing
